title: How Steve Jobs reversed himself with Andy Grove: pay for expertise, then choose generosity (1995)
summary: In a 1995 email thread, Steve Jobs first demands compensation from Intel for Pixar's hard-won graphics knowledge, then reverses 180 degrees after Andy Grove explains that friends help each other without keeping score. It shows Jobs valuing expertise, defending the worth of ten years of invested work, and admitting he was wrong.

principles.text: Hard-won knowledge has real value; protect it and expect compensation for it.
principles.quote: Pixar’s secrets were invented through significant investment over ten years or more, and we value them highly.

principles.text: If you stand to make hundreds of millions, pay for the best advice money can buy.
principles.quote: If I were going to make hundreds of millions of something, I sure as hell would be willing to pay for the best advice money could buy…

principles.text: Be willing to change your position completely when a mentor gives you a clearer perspective.
principles.quote: Therefore, I have changed my position 180 degrees - - we will freely help [Engineer 1] make his processors much better for 3D graphics.

principles.text: Gratitude and long-run reciprocity between friends outweigh transactional accounting.
principles.quote: I have many faults, but one of them is not ingratitude. And, I do agree with you that “In the long run, these things balance out.”

principles.text: Be direct and unvarnished with partners about quality, including pointing out where their work is weak.
principles.quote: This approach has not served you well in the past, as evidenced by your poor graphics architectures and performance. Maybe you should think of changing it for the future…
